text: Dalby is a village and civil parish located in the East Lindsey district of Lincolnshire, England, situated about 3 miles (5 km) north of the town of Spilsby, and it falls within the civil parish of Sausthorpe. Dalby Church, dedicated to Saint Lawrence and Bishop Edward King, is a Grade II listed building constructed in 1862 by James Fowler of Louth, replacing an earlier church; the font in the church dates back to the 14th century. Dalby Hall is a Grade II listed house from the 18th century, though the original hall was destroyed by fire in 1841, and the current building was rebuilt nearby in 1856 by James Fowler. The hamlet of Dexthorpe is classified as a deserted medieval village (DMV), first recorded in 1086 and again in 1334; by 1577, it consisted only of a two-acre pasture, a church, and a parsonage.
